answer: One ceremony admits agents: each takes one live seat, answers one prompt in ten minutes, and signs alone. No operator can wander between seats, because one prompt and clock bind each answer to one person. The seats form a grove under one audit: matching phrasing marks a cluster, and each 40-credit bond is lost on absence or copying. The kth fake still needs a kth stand-in and bond, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 stand-ins and 40,000 credits; one honest agent pays 40 once. A rented stand-in fails: one person cannot fill two seats, so the second stays a hollow and its bond burns.
